title: AquaSentinel: Uncertainty-Aware Groundwater Contamination Modelling and Adaptive Environmental Sampling
abstract: A proposed spatial data science investigation exploring whether probabilistic models can estimate groundwater contamination risk, quantify predictive uncertainty and identify locations where additional environmental sampling would be most informative. The initial research will focus on Bihar and a single scientifically justified contaminant, subject to authentic groundwater chemistry data availability.
content:
## Research Motivation

Groundwater monitoring measurements are spatially incomplete. Conventional contamination prediction maps may obscure uncertainty and provide insufficient guidance on where additional measurements would improve environmental knowledge.

## Primary Research Question

Can spatial probabilistic models estimate groundwater contamination risk, quantify predictive uncertainty and identify locations where additional sampling would provide the greatest improvement in environmental knowledge?

## Initial Scope

Begin in Bihar with one contaminant, preferably arsenic if sufficient geographically referenced observations are available. Do not expand to multiple contaminants before validating the initial methodology.

## Proposed Methodology

- Audit authentic groundwater chemistry measurements and associated metadata.
- Investigate spatial coverage, reporting limits, missingness, measurement uncertainty and temporal variation.
- Establish classical spatial interpolation baselines.
- Evaluate ordinary Kriging and Gaussian Process Regression.
- Investigate Bayesian hierarchical spatial models where justified.
- Quantify predictive uncertainty and assess calibration.
- Establish geographically separated evaluation regions.
- Compare uncertainty-guided sampling with random and spatially balanced sampling strategies.

## Candidate Datasets

Central Ground Water Board observations, National Water Data Portal groundwater chemistry datasets, Jal Jeevan Mission water-quality records and relevant geological and hydrological data. Feasibility remains subject to audit.

## Proposed Technology Stack

Python, PyMC, ArviZ, GPyTorch, SciPy, GeoPandas, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and Plotly.

## Evaluation Strategy

Predictive error, probabilistic scoring metrics, interval coverage, uncertainty calibration, spatial generalization and simulated sampling efficiency.

## Scientific Limitations

Predicted contamination maps are research estimates, not certified drinking-water safety assessments. Missing observations cannot establish safe water. Adaptive sampling will initially be evaluated using withheld measurements or documented simulations.

## Current Status

Research proposal established. Dataset acquisition, implementation and experimental evaluation have not started.
